channel.title: RiskLens Australia: News and regulatory updates
channel.description: Plain-English news and commentary on Australian risk, compliance and governance.

item.title: Third cyber penalty for a licensee: Fortnum Private Wealth
item.description: A financial advice licensee has been penalised $1.35 million for failing to manage cyber security risk across its network of advice practices, the third such outcome for ASIC.

item.title: Super fund valuations: ASIC says trustees and auditors must dig deeper
item.description: ASIC's second review of super fund financial reporting and audit found continuing weaknesses in how unlisted investments are valued and checked, and a reminder that trustees can't hand that responsibility to fund managers.

item.title: Regulatory roundup: mid-October 2026
item.description: The main Australian risk, compliance and governance developments from 1 to 22 October 2026, and what's coming up next.

item.title: Insurance claims in the spotlight: a first utmost good faith penalty
item.description: An insurer has been penalised for the first time for breaching the duty of utmost good faith, over a home insurance claim that took more than three years to finalise.

item.title: Regulatory roundup: winter 2026
item.description: The main Australian risk, compliance and governance developments from June to September 2026, and what's coming up next.

item.title: Platform trustees in the spotlight: what ASIC's Report 833 means
item.description: ASIC's review of super platform trustees found persistent gaps in the controls meant to stop members' savings being drained by harmful advice fees, risky switching and unusual investments. The lessons reach well beyond platforms.

item.title: APRA's governance reset: what draft CPS 510 would change
item.description: APRA wants one governance standard for banks, insurers and super trustees. The draft would tighten rules on tenure, board make-up and conflicts, and is the biggest shake-up of prudential governance in more than a decade.
